thread:
maria (oncall): Incident bot paged on SSE disconnects impacting function-calls. seeing spikes in 502s from the streaming gateway. anyone oncall?
incident-bot: Pager duty alert: SEV2 - streaming gateway SSE disconnect rate > 15% across us-west-2 for the last 7m. Paging @maria (oncall).
ash (client-ops-bot): FYI a few customers reported tool call failures around 21:03 UTC.
mar ia (oncall): I saw that. triaging now. first pass: many of the failures are 'invalid-json' from tool-call parser, but payloads look cut off.
sam: are these from a specific client version or across all?
maria (oncall): early signal shows a cluster of requests with header `x-client-proto: seq-v2` and some without. suspected mismatch in client streaming framing.
deepak: logging bucket: s3://redwood-logs/prod/streaming/us-west-2/21111122/ . pulled a sample. here's one truncated chunk:```
POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: inference.redwood.ai
Content-Type: text/event-stream
x-client-proto: seq-v2

data: {"type":"toolcall","id":"t-9a3","payload":"{\"fn\":\"lookup\",\"args\":{\"q\":\"us\"}"
```
lisa: that looks like the client closed mid-event. do we see network timeouts upstream?
ash (client-ops-bot): tcp reset rates on the edge proxy spiked at the same time window.
ashley: which versions of the gateway rolled recently? any deploys?
maria (oncall): no deploys in that window per eng-releases channel. runtime autoscaler did trigger scale events earlier at 20:58 due to a traffic burst.
sam: hypothesis 1: autoscaler scale events briefly drained connections and some clients retry incorrectly causing half-formed SSE messages. hypothesis 2: new client builds (seq-v2) changed chunking/flush semantics and some proxies close idle connections faster.
deepak: building a timeline now. 20:57: autoscale trigger. 21:02: first customer reported failure. 21:03-21:10: disconnect spike / 502s. 21:12: mitigation started (canary route to fallback polling).
lisa: can we reproduce locally with the seq-v2 client emulator? I have a script to send intentionally fragmented SSE chunks.
ash: sending note to customers flagged: "We're investigating intermittent tool-call failures from streaming sessions; temporary fallback to non-streaming route enabled for affected requests."
mar ia (oncall): live mitigation: routing policy updated to prefer long-poll for clients with x-client-proto missing or seq-v2 for 10m. rolling back after 21:40 decreased error rate to baseline.
sam: good. we should capture full logs for the affected connection ids. deepak, can you grep for t- ids and attach a short timeline per ID?
deepak: pulled a few ids and their connection logs (trimmed):
```
conn-84321: accept -> auth -> sse-open -> data chunk (len 512) -> data chunk (len 128) -> connection-close (RST) -> parser error: unexpected EOF
conn-84999: accept -> sse-open -> data chunk (len 1024) -> data chunk (len 0) -> parser error: invalid json at offset 1023
```
ashley: parser error at offset 1023 sounds like a boundary problem, maybe an off-by-one in the chunk assembly code. which library is assembling SSE frames?
mar ia (oncall): runtime uses internal stream-assembler v3.4.2. approx 70% of failing connections were on nodes running v3.4.2; others on earlier versions didn't show the same error profile.
sam: that suggests a runtime regression in how we buffer chunks for SSE messages. Deepak, can you run `strings` on the binary and confirm build tag?
deepak: confirmed nodes with v3.4.2 were built at 2026-03-01 03:12 UTC.
lisa: ok reproduce plan: emulate seq-v2 client that sends split JSON across SSE events in multiple small chunks with a delayed flush. run against a node with v3.4.2 and one with v3.3.x.
incide nt-bot: Reminder: add customer impact numbers to the incident doc.
maria (oncall): customer impact: approx 120 requests/min failed for 8m window; 6 customers saw degraded function-call behavior (two reported timeouts in prod). CS notified.
sam: assign owners: runtime-team -> investigate stream-assembler change (deepak), devex -> coordinate client-emulator (lisa), oncall -> continue mitigation and customer comms (maria).
nash: also capture network proxy metrics (timeouts, rst) and any kube node reboots in that window.
deepak: quick diff of stream-assembler between v3.4.1 and v3.4.2 shows introduced optimization: `if (chunk_len % 1024 == 0) fast-path = true` which bypasses a copy; looks suspicious.
lisa: that code path could let partial JSON align to buffer edges incorrectly if the client yields differently. reproducing now.
(10m later)
lisa: reproduced locally: when client emits 512b + 512b with a tiny delay, v3.4.2 assembler sometimes emits incomplete last buffer - parser gets EOF. v3.3.x works.
sam: mitigation decision: revert the fast-path on all affected nodes and redeploy a hotfix build v3.4.3, and keep the long-poll fallback for 30m to smooth customers.
maria (oncall): I've queued a rollback patch for the runtime pool and triggered rolling restart of the affected nodes. patches will roll over 6 minutes.
nash: sent updated note to customers: "Hotfix in progress; temporary fallback to polling remains active. We'll update when fully resolved."
ashley: add test case to stream-assembler unit tests for boundary-aligned chunking and delayed flush.
deepak: pushing hotfix branch now. patch includes disabling the fast-path and an extra assert for chunk assembly. will coordinate with eng-releases for expedited rollout.
mar ia (oncall): monitoring: error rate dropped back to normal after nodes replaced with v3.4.3 at 21:33.
incide nt-bot: Incident SEV2 resolved. postmortem required within 72h.
sam: next steps in-thread: - attach raw logs for scrubbed connections (done) - write RCA hypothesis summary - assign follow-ups (runtime fix shipped, tests added, release gating for asm optimizations) - schedule post-incident blameless review.
maria (oncall): I'll open the incident doc and paste timeline + hypothesis table. assigning runtime/stream-assembler owner to add code link.
lisa: client side: we'll add compatibility tests and a note to client SDK docs about flush semantics for seq-v2.
nash: ops will follow up with the two customers who reported timeouts to confirm service once hotfix in.
ashley: one more ask: add an eval that simulates high connection churn while autoscaling to ensure assembler robustness under scale.
sam: agreed. thanks all for the quick coordination. closing live mitigation. we'll capture the full RCA in the incident doc.
nash (client-ops-bot): customers updated.
maria (oncall): closing thread here; I'll post the incident doc link when available. thanks everyone.
